answer: An identity joins the island registry by locking 60 credits and running a service endpoint probed by knoll auditors; the jetty log timestamps probes, and a missed or wrong-key reply forfeits the bond. One fake endpoint costs 85 credits, a second 90, a third 95, each one adding 5, as shared hosts are flagged. Across 1,000 fake endpoints the bill reaches 2,582,500 credits. A rented hosting farm fails: shared addresses make probes miss together, and auditors burn every bond in the cluster. A genuine operator posts one 60-credit bond for its endpoint and recovers it after one clean epoch.
